# BrainBro

> A self-hosted second brain for people and their AI assistants. Drop it now, sort it later.

BrainBro is a private notes and knowledge app that runs on your own server. It
keeps one shared memory that you and your assistants can read and update. Notes
start in the inbox; organize them into collections when useful. Boards are
another view over the same items.

## Connecting an AI assistant

- MCP endpoint: `https://<your BrainBro host>/api/mcp`
- Remote transport: Streamable HTTP.
- Authentication: sign in through BrainBro with OAuth (recommended), or use a
  personal API token as a bearer token. An OAuth connection is limited to MCP;
  a personal token acts as the user across the REST API.
- Setup steps for Claude, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok and
  other MCP clients: [docs/mcp.md](https://github.com/TheBrainBro/brainbro/blob/main/docs/mcp.md).
- The host must be reachable by remote clients over HTTPS. The local
  development server is not reachable from hosted assistants.

## How to use BrainBro

- Search before capturing: check whether the information is already saved.
- Capture requested memories as titled notes and leave them in the inbox unless
  the user asks to organize them.
- Read a note before editing it. Use its returned version and prefer a partial
  edit so existing content is preserved; retry by reading again if the version
  is stale.
- Use search results only when they are relevant. Search can return loose
  semantic matches; never reveal unrelated notes.
- Organize, archive, or place items on boards only when asked.
- BrainBro has no delete tool. Only the user can restore an older revision in
  the app.
- Be clear about what you read, saved, or changed. Never claim an action
  succeeded if the tool returned an error.
